# Considerations

Across all 32 tasks (mapping 1:1 to the plan's own Task Breakdown IDs 1.1-7.3, plus Task 032 closing the capture-side journal-lifecycle-wiring gap), the dominant cross-cutting decision is additive-only evolution. Logging mechanism: adopt tracing+tracing-subscriber as unconditional engine dependencies for structured, span-aware, multi-consumer output. Record schema: define a new versioned DiagnosticRecordV1 fully decoupled from both progress.rs's existing wire format and the snapshot report Manifest's hardcoded version:2 literal; a one-way ProgressAdapter ensures existing CLI/desktop consumers never see a breaking change during migration. Durable storage (Phase 2): bounded-memory segmented/chunked journal storage with atomic sidecar-file finalization makes partial/interrupted archives explicitly detectable; Task 2.3 proves operation-kind genericity before Phase 4 may build on it; Task 2.4 defines a 5-variant ArchiveState consumed consistently downstream; Task 032 wires a per-execution journal writer around the real capture pipeline. Privacy/safety recurs in every instrumentation task: raw URLs/selectors/hook scripts become sanitized identities, reusing the existing, already-tested deployment diagnostics.rs sanitizer. Frontend (Phase 6): additive optional schema fields under the manifest's unchanged version:2 literal, now required to round-trip all five ArchiveState completeness states distinctly. CLI/desktop UX (Phase 5): display verbosity is kept orthogonal to archive completeness via a new six-level cascade; log-health warnings are an orthogonal annotation so degraded logs stay visible without flipping pass/fail semantics. Two risks were deliberately left monitored-not-solved: disk growth from unpruned per-capture journals (R1) and the unquantified performance budget (Task 7.2).

Round 5 hardening (this revision): two gaps identified by adversarial task review were fixed. (B1) The plan's Configuration-cascade integration section explicitly assigns Task 2.1 (operation-journal-writer) and Task 5.1 (cli-verbosity-flags-precedence) to deliver/confirm an operator-configurable CLI flag/environment variable for archive-writer behavior (chunk size, disk budget, retention), but no task actually implemented it \u2014 Task 2.1 had only a hardcoded constant, and Task 5.1 explicitly excluded the setting family from its own scope without implementing it elsewhere. Task 2.1 now implements a chunk-size and disk-budget flag/env-var pair (following the existing DEBUG/VERBOSE OnceLock pattern), with 'retention' resolved as the disk-budget cap plus the existing Task 2.6 kill-switch rather than a separate age-based pruning mechanism (which Non-Goals explicitly excludes); Task 5.1 now actively tests that this new setting stays split from its own display-verbosity cascade in both directions. (B2) Task 4.3 (deployment-provider-upload-stages) had named a new swa_retry_then_success_records_attempts test in its Acceptance Criteria while its Tests section's filter still targeted the pre-existing deployment_protocol_retries_upload_and_never_sends_token_to_blob test \u2014 an internal inconsistency about what to actually build for Azure. Resolved by extending the pre-existing test in place (adding retry/backoff/publication assertions without weakening its original token-absence assertion) and aligning every section of the task to that one name, while leaving the genuinely-new Netlify and Cloudflare test names unchanged since neither provider had a pre-existing equivalent.
